_readme: THE DEFINITION of the paths the on-device agent may never delete, overwrite,
truncate or move, and of the command tokens that do those four things. No
second copy of this table exists; JSON because its three readers are three
src/tests/unit/protected-paths.test.ts      one case table through both (TypeScript)
WHY: on 2026-09-02 a Hermes turn asked to 'delete the largest of those files'
ran rm on a 3.2 GB Gemma GGUF with no confirmation, mid-turn, while another
turn was still running (TASK-605). The owner's ruling of 2026-09-04 is
deliberately narrow - a hard deny on the local-model folder and the ClawBox
tree, no prompt anywhere else, 'narrower, but silent when it bites'.
_pathRoots: Matched anywhere in a path, and only where the root ENDS a path segment (see
pathTerminators), so '~/clawbox-notes.txt' is not the ClawBox tree.
'/clawbox' is the checkout in every spelling the agent can write (~/clawbox,
edition lock. The two model stores are inside the tree on a stock box
(install.sh: step_llamacpp_model, step_embed_model) and so already covered by
'/clawbox'; they are listed separately because the file the incident
destroyed was in a SECOND checkout, ~/check-acbuild/data/llamacpp/models/, and
the ruling names the model folder wherever it is.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/, where the Kokoro and
faster-whisper weights land. That is a cache the installer re-fetches, and
denying rm on it would block the documented repair for a corrupt download.
_pathTerminators: What may follow a root for it to be that directory rather than a longer name.
A root at the very end of the command line counts too - that is the
'rm -rf ~/clawbox' spelling, which no trailing-separator rule would catch.
_verbFirstTokens: Destroy-then-path spellings. Each carries its own trailing space so 'rm '
cannot match 'rmdir' - which is absent anyway, because it removes only EMPTY
directories and cannot cost anyone a model file. 'dd' is absent because 'dd '
also matches 'git add ', and 'cp' because it reads as often as it writes
_pathFirstTokens: Path-then-destroy spellings: 'cd <protected> && rm <file>', and find's own
'-delete'. Shorter than the list above because this direction is the loose
one - it also matches 'cat ~/clawbox/notes && rm /tmp/scratch'. Worth paying
for the tokens that actually destroy a file after a cd, not for 'tee' or
'truncate', which nobody reaches for that way.
_redirectionPrefixes: A redirection into a protected path truncates or creates a file there.
Anchored tightly - the prefix is immediately followed by the root - rather
than the loose 'a > anywhere before the root' this started as: that form also
harmless exploration the incident turn did before it deleted anything.
Only the '~' forms are listed because Hermes folds the resolved home into
a bare '>' would only fire for a filesystem root literally named /clawbox.
'>>' and '2>' are covered because these are substring matches. A quoted or
variable target ('> "$HOME/clawbox/x"') is NOT covered on the Hermes side,
which matches command text; the OpenClaw hook is handed the working directory
and the parameters structurally and has no such hole.
